items.title: Section: Mind-Reading — Every State a Mind Can Be In, and a Debate on How "Other-Minds" Knowledge Is Even Possible

items.zh: 謂佛菩薩以他心智，遍知十方無量無數諸世界中他有情類，若有纏煩惱心，若離纏煩惱心，若有隨縛、有隨眠煩惱心，若離隨縛、離隨眠煩惱心。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, through the wisdom of knowing others' minds, universally know, throughout the ten directions' immeasurable, uncountable worlds, whether another being's mind is presently gripped by affliction or free of it in the moment, and whether it still carries the underlying bonds and latent seeds of affliction or is genuinely free of them.

items.zh: 又遍了知有染心、邪願心，謂諸外道心及有愛染心。又遍了知無染心、正願心，謂與上相違心。又遍了知劣心，謂生欲界諸有情類，下至一切禽獸等心。又遍了知中心，謂生色界諸有情類諸所有心。又遍了知勝心，謂生無色界諸有情類諸所有心。又遍了知樂相應心、苦相應心、不苦不樂相應心。又能以一知他心智，於一有情如是所有、如是體性、如是品類、如是行相、如是分齊心起現前，於一念頃並如實知。又能以一知他心智，於多有情如是所有、如是體性、如是品類、如是行相、如是分齊心起現前，於一念頃並如實知。又佛菩薩此他心通，知諸有情諸根勝劣，知諸有情種種勝解，知諸有情種種界行，隨其所應，能正安處趣涅槃宮種種正行。
items.en: With a single act of knowing others' minds, they truly know, for a single being or for countless beings alike, the exact affliction present, its wholesome or unwholesome character, its grade of intensity, how it arose with respect to its object, and whether it belongs to an unenlightened or noble mind — all within a single instant. ... Through this same knowledge of others' minds, buddhas and bodhisattvas know beings' faculties, strong or weak, their manifold degrees of understanding, and their manifold underlying dispositions, and accordingly are able to correctly guide each towards whatever practice actually leads them to nirvāṇa.

items.zh: 當知是名此所作業。云何諸佛菩薩漏盡智通？

items.title: Section: Why a Bodhisattva Knows How to End All Affliction, Yet Deliberately Does Not

items.zh: 謂佛菩薩如實了知煩惱盡得，如實了知若自、若他於諸漏盡已得未得，如實了知若自、若他所有能得漏盡方便。如能如實了知方便，於非方便亦如實知。如實知他於漏盡得有增上慢，如實知他於漏盡得離增上慢。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas truly know the attainment of extinguishing contaminants; they truly know, for themselves or others, whether the extinction of contaminants has been attained or not yet attained; they truly know, for themselves or others, the actual means for attaining it ... they truly know when another holds a presumptuous overestimation regarding their own attainment of this extinction, and truly know when another is genuinely free of such overestimation.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，雖能如實了知一切漏盡功德能證方便，而不作證。是故菩薩於有漏事及與諸漏不速捨離；雖行種種有漏事中，而不染污。如是威力，於諸威力最為殊勝。
items.en: Moreover, bodhisattvas, although able to truly know every virtue of extinguishing contaminants and the very means to realise it, do not actually realise it. For this reason, bodhisattvas do not swiftly abandon conditioned, contaminated existence and its contaminants — and though they move through the very midst of contaminated affairs, they remain undefiled by them. This power, among all the powers described, is the most excellent of all.

items.title: All Six Superknowledges Close; the Power of the Dharma Reopens With Ten Perfections

items.zh: 又佛菩薩由漏盡智，自無染污；亦善為他廣分別說，壞增上慢。當知是名此所作業。
items.en: Moreover, through this wisdom of extinguishing contaminants, buddhas and bodhisattvas remain themselves undefiled, and are also able to skilfully and thoroughly explain this to others, dismantling any presumptuous overestimation. This should be understood as its function.

items.title: The Dharma's Power Has Four Faces for Every Perfection

items.zh: 云何法威力？謂布施威力乃至般若威力。此布施等諸法威力，應知一一略有四相。一者、斷所對治相，二者、資糧成熟相，三者、饒益自他相，四者、與當來果相。
items.en: What is the power of the Dharma? It is the power of giving, up through the power of wisdom. It should be understood that each of these practices — giving and the rest — has, in brief, four aspects: first, breaking what it directly opposes; second, ripening the provisions towards awakening; third, benefiting oneself and others; and fourth, yielding a specific future fruit.

items.title: Giving's Four Powers — From Breaking Stinginess to a Future of Effortless Abundance

items.zh: 布施四相者，謂諸菩薩修行惠施，能斷慳悋，施所對治。是名第一。即此惠施，能作自己菩提資糧，亦即能作布施攝事成熟有情。是名第二。施先意悅，施時心淨，施已無悔，於三時中心常歡喜，以自饒益；亦能除他飢渴、寒熱、種種疾病、所欲匱乏、怖畏眾苦，以饒益他。
items.en: Giving's four aspects: bodhisattvas who practice giving are able to break stinginess, the very thing giving directly opposes. ... Before giving, the mind delights; while giving, the mind is pure; after giving, there is no regret — across all three times, the mind remains constantly joyful, benefiting oneself; and it removes others' hunger, thirst, cold, heat, various illness, want, and fearful suffering, benefiting others.

items.zh: 於當來世在在生處，恒常富樂，得大祿位、得大財寶、得大朋黨、得大眷屬。
items.en: In whatever place they are reborn in future lives, they constantly enjoy wealth and ease, attaining high position, great riches, capable companions, and a great and noble family.

items.zh: 是名第四。是名布施威力四相。此外無有若過若增。

items.title: Moral Discipline's Four Powers — Sleeping Safely Under a Guardian's Watch

items.zh: 持戒四相者，謂諸菩薩受持清淨身語律儀，能斷犯戒，戒所對治。是名第一。即所受持清淨尸羅，能為自己菩提資糧，亦即能作同事攝事成熟有情。是名第二。受持淨戒，捨離犯戒為緣所生怖畏、眾罪、怨敵等事，寢寤安樂，以自饒益。
items.en: Moral discipline's four aspects: bodhisattvas who uphold pure conduct of body and speech are able to break transgression, the very thing discipline directly opposes. ... Upholding pure discipline, they are freed from the fear, wrongdoing, and hostility that transgression would otherwise produce, resting easily whether waking or sleeping, benefiting themselves.

items.zh: 又由淨戒、無悔、歡喜乃至心定，以自饒益；受持淨戒，不損惱他，普施一切有情無畏，以饒益他。是名第三。
由是因緣，身壞已後。生於善趣天世界中。
items.en: By this cause, once the body has perished, they are reborn among the heavens, a favourable realm.

items.zh: 是名第四。是名持戒威力四相。此外無有若過若增。

blocks.text: The last two superknowledges, including a striking point: bodhisattvas know how to end the contaminants, but deliberately do not, yet. Then the power of the perfections.

"Whether another's mind is gripped by affliction or free of it in the moment, and whether it still carries the latent seeds." Venerable Miào Jìng: on the surface a mind may look pure, but inside the seeds remain. "With a single act of knowing", for one being or countless, they know the affliction, its grade, and how it arose.
They know for themselves and others whether it has been attained, and they recognise "presumptuous overestimation": claiming attainments one lacks. Master Cháng Bǎi explains overestimation.

"Bodhisattvas, although able to truly know every virtue of extinguishing contaminants and the means to realise it, do not actually realise it." So "they do not swiftly abandon conditioned, contaminated existence", because they stay to help beings. Master Cháng Bǎi comments.
Each perfection has four powers: it breaks what it opposes; it ripens the provisions for awakening; it benefits self and others; it brings future fruit.
It breaks stinginess. "Before giving the mind delights; while giving it is pure; after giving there is no regret." In future lives, "wealth and ease, high position, capable companions".
It breaks transgression; "freed from fear, worry, and regret", one sleeps safely; "reborn among the heavens".

quiz.q: Knowing minds "gripped by affliction … carrying latent seeds." How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide the two parts?
options: first manifest afflictions, then their seeds
quiz.why: "Whether another being's mind is presently gripped by affliction or free of it in the moment, and whether it still carries the underlying bonds and latent seeds of affliction." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first part explains manifest afflictions; the latter stresses their seeds.

quiz.q: "A mind with latent afflictions" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: outwardly pure, but holding affliction seeds within
quiz.why: "Whether it still carries the underlying bonds and latent seeds of affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: on the surface his mind looks pure, but inside there are seeds of affliction.

quiz.q: Knowing "when another overestimates their extinction of contaminants." How do the masters explain this overestimation?
options: both: misreading the signs — taking dhyāna for the noble path, the first dhyāna for stream-entry
quiz.why: "They truly know when another holds a presumptuous overestimation regarding their own attainment of this extinction." Master Cháng Bǎi: overestimation is misreading the signs — taking dhyāna for the noble path, the first dhyāna for the first fruit. Venerable Miào Jìng: not having the first fruit but thinking one has it; not having concentration but thinking one has it — that's overestimation.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas know the means to extinguish contaminants "yet don't realise it." Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: cutting all affliction seeds would leave no channel for connecting with beings
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, although able to truly know every virtue of extinguishing contaminants and the very means to realise it, do not actually realise it." Master Cháng Bǎi: if all affliction seeds were cut, there'd be no channel left for forming bonds with beings.

quiz.q: Each perfection has four aspects; first, "breaking what it opposes." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: each perfection cuts off the affliction it opposes
quiz.why: "First, breaking what it directly opposes; second, ripening the provisions towards awakening; third, benefiting oneself and others; and fourth, yielding a specific future fruit." Master Cháng Bǎi: first, breaking what it opposes — each of the six perfections has the aspect of cutting off the affliction it counters.

quiz.q: "Before giving, delight; while giving, purity; after, no regret." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain purity while giving?
options: the mind is pure while giving — relying on nothing, seeking nothing
quiz.why: "Before giving, the mind delights; while giving, the mind is pure; after giving, there is no regret." Master Cháng Bǎi: while giving, the mind is very pure — relying on nothing, seeking nothing.

quiz.q: Discipline's future fruit: "reborn among the heavens." What does Master Cháng Bǎi add?
options: discipline can bring heaven; if one vows to return as a human, that too
quiz.why: "By this cause, once the body has perished, they are reborn among the heavens, a favourable realm." Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping precepts can bring heavenly rebirth; if one vows to come back as a human, one can be human too.
